what_this_is: DATA for read-data/settings.mjs and read-data/settings.py, the one shared reader of a person's tool settings. A setting is one row of the person's generic Settings list (`list`), row type `row_type`, kept as the record type `record_type` with the id `<id_prefix><tool folder><separator><scope kind><separator><scope id>`. `scope_kinds`: what a setting may be for. `fields`: the fields of a setting row's value; `settings` holds the tool's own settings as one JSON object (or that object as JSON text). Only a row whose `status` is `active_status` is read. `words`: every refusal, {name} filled from the call.

words.bad_id: settings_record must be a setting id `record:setting:<tool folder>~<scope kind>~<scope id>` (scope kind one of {kinds}); got {id}.
words.bad_scope_kind: The setting {id} names scope kind {scope_kind}; it must be one of {kinds}.
words.other_tool: The setting {id} is for the tool {owner}, not {tool}. Send this tool's own setting.
words.missing: The person has no setting {id}. Add it as a row of list:settings (record type record:setting) with tool, scope_kind, scope_id and settings, then run again.
words.not_active: The setting {id} has status {status}; only an active setting is read. Mark it active or send another setting.
words.value_tool: The setting {id} says it is for the tool {owner}, but its id names {tool}. Fix the row so both name one tool.
words.bad_settings: The setting {id} holds no settings object in `settings` (an object, or that object as JSON text). Fix the row.
words.no_door: Reading the setting {id} needs the person's records door; this run was not handed one. Declare a records:read right on record:setting for that id.
words.bad_part: A setting's {field} must be text without `~` or `/`; got {value}.
